## Purpose

A `Mode` enum encodes the closed set of enforcement levels a Task/Write hook can run at — typically `Off`/`Warn`/`Strict` or `Observe`/`Warn`/`Strict`. Each hook owns its mode privately (`enum ...Mode`, not shared), resolved from its own env var with a documented default. The three exemplars (`context_budget_gate.rs`, `delegation_advisory.rs`, `main_context_counter.rs`) all read the mode BEFORE doing any measurement, so an `Off` mode short-circuits cheaply. Advisory hooks (`delegation_advisory`) never define a `Strict` variant at all — only enforcement hooks (`context_budget_gate`, `main_context_counter`) do.

## Convention

Folder: apps/rt/src/hooks/task/**, apps/rt/src/hooks/write/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 7

A mode enum is `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]`, private to its module (no `pub`), with a `fn mode() -> Mode` (or a name-prefixed variant like `context_budget_mode()`) that reads `std::env::var("MUSTARD_..._MODE")` — an unset or unrecognised value always falls back to the module's documented default, never `Strict` unless the module says so explicitly. The three exemplars each document the fallback rule in a doc-comment directly above the resolver function.

## How to apply

Add the enum and its resolver function near the top of the hook module, right after its constants. Give the mode's env var name a comment stating what an absent/unrecognised value resolves to, and wire the resolver into the `Check`/`Observer` entry point before any measurement or IO — mirroring `context_budget_mode()` in `context_budget_gate.rs` and `mode()` in `delegation_advisory.rs`.

## Examples

Ref: apps/rt/src/hooks/task/delegation_advisory.rs
Ref: apps/rt/src/hooks/task/main_context_counter.rs
Ref: apps/rt/src/hooks/task/context_budget_gate.rs

```rust
/// The `MUSTARD_DELEGATION_WARN_MODE` mode. Mirrors the sibling gates' shape.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum Mode {
    /// Disabled — pure no-op.
    Off,
    /// Surface the advisory (default).
    Warn,
}

/// Resolve the mode from `MUSTARD_DELEGATION_WARN_MODE` (default `warn`). Only
/// `off` disables it; anything else (incl. unset) is `warn` — this is advisory,
/// there is no `strict`/blocking mode by design.
fn mode() -> Mode {
    match std::env::var("MUSTARD_DELEGATION_WARN_MODE")
        .unwrap_or_default()
        .to_ascii_lowercase()
        .as_str()
    {
        "off" => Mode::Off,
        _ => Mode::Warn,
    }
}
```
